shapes.text: leading strand: grows towards the fork
lagging strand: grows away, in pieces

dna_replication.caption: The direction problem. Grey: the old strands, running opposite ways. A polymerase only adds to a 3′ end (arrowheads), so the leading strand grows towards the fork and the lagging strand away from it, restarted in pieces as the fork uncovers template. Not to scale.

bars.label: after proofreading (range 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁸; bar at the middle)
mutation rate per base pair per generation, yeast, mismatch repair absent
mutation rate per base pair per generation, yeast, mismatch repair present

rep_fidelity.caption: Each check removes most of the errors left by the one before. Base selection: about 1 error in 10⁴ to 10⁵ (the bar shows 10⁻⁵); Pol α, which cannot proofread, about 10⁻⁴. Proofreading improves fidelity 10 to 1,000-fold, so the third bar is 10⁻⁵ divided by 10 to 1,000, a calculated range. The two lower bars are a different measure, from another organism: mutations per base pair per generation in yeast cells without and with mismatch repair (Lujan and others 2014). Sources on the card.

RNA primer removal, human proteins (test tube)

rep_okazaki.caption: How fast the parts go. The fork in HeLa cells averages 0.68 kb a minute (Guilbaud and others 2011). Pol δ figures from Burgers and Kunkel 2017; primer removal by Pol δ and FEN1 with purified human proteins takes about 11 s a nucleotide (Raducanu and others 2022), so cells must have a faster way. E. coli figure from OpenStax Biology.
